summary: SinkCast (K=1) fails all three success criteria. The localization premise is refuted (D_logit(0) accounts for only 5-9% of total shift-error, far below the 50% threshold). Microbenchmark gap closure peaks at 36.3% (Mistral K=1) and 23.6% (Llama K=4), well below the 80% target. Downstream accuracy improvement averages -0.91 points overall, with BF16 position-shift degradation already near zero, leaving no signal for SinkCast to improve.
analysis: Three-part evaluation: (1) Localization: D_logit(0)/sum(D_logit) = 4.9% (Llama) and 8.2% (Mistral) across all configurations, consistently the smallest among 5 sampled key indices. The BF16 shift-error is broadly distributed, not concentrated at the sink key. (2) Microbenchmark: Best gap closure is 36.3% (Mistral K=1) and 23.6% (Llama K=4). Even correcting all keys (K=S) in a single layer achieves only ~26.5%, revealing an inherent ceiling from FlashAttention's tiled BF16 accumulation. K>4 degrades Llama results. (3) Downstream: BF16 drops are already <1 point on average across RULER and LongBench. SinkCast does not reduce these drops; the overall average improvement is -0.91 (slightly worse). The only +2.09 result (Llama RULER QA 8192) is confounded by SinkCast changing d=0 accuracy from 11.59 to 46.34. On Mistral RULER, SinkCast increases shift-sensitivity by 2.85 points on average. Two optimization iterations fixed real bugs but could not change the fundamental outcome.
reason: The verdict is 'bad' because all three criteria fail due to fundamental limitations, not implementation bugs: (1) The core premise that shift-error is localized at the sink key (j=0) is empirically refuted -- error is uniformly distributed across keys. (2) The correction approach has an inherent ceiling (~26-36% gap closure) because FlashAttention's tiled BF16 accumulation introduces errors that per-key logit correction cannot address. (3) BF16 position-shift degradation on downstream tasks is already negligible, providing no signal for SinkCast to improve. These are structural limitations of the approach, not tunable parameters. Two optimization iterations confirmed this: both fixed genuine bugs but neither moved the fundamental metrics toward the success thresholds.
